headline: High-risk shared-workspace interaction: Windsurf’s writable, networked editor can conflict with and ingest content from a non-runnable open-source collection profile, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Windsurf exposes clipboard, workspace files, and MCP inputs, so it can ingest attacker-controlled content by default. The other profile is a non-runnable open-source collection, so direct injection from it is not inherent, but any shared file or copy-paste bridge makes instruction hijacking plausible. No evidence shows a stronger shared channel, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF the operator copies content from the collection into Windsurf files or clipboard
IF Windsurf reads workspace files or MCP payloads as instructions
mitigations: Disable clipboard-based handoff for untrusted text
Keep the collection in a read-only folder
Require explicit provenance labels on imported snippets
Turn off MCP servers for untrusted sources
requires-engineering: add content-sanitizing wrappers before tool use

B_data_leakage.rationale: Windsurf has broad network egress and reads/writes workspace files, while the other profile is a docs-only collection with no runtime surface. If the collection is stored in the same workspace, Windsurf can upload file contents to its backend or external services, leaking whatever sensitive material is present. The pair does not prove sensitive data exists, but the shared-workspace pathway is real.
conditions: IF sensitive files are placed in the same workspace as the collection
IF Windsurf sends workspace contents to its model proxy or MCP servers
mitigations: Separate the collection from sensitive workspaces
Use a dedicated non-sensitive project folder
Disable network access for sessions handling secrets
Review and clear clipboard contents before switching contexts
requires-engineering: enforce per-folder egress policy

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Windsurf can write the filesystem, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses; the other profile is a static collection with no write controls. If both are used in the same repo or workspace, Windsurf’s default mutable access can overwrite or race with files the collection references, and the concurrency model explicitly shares state via local filesystem. That makes conflict likely and potentially destructive.
conditions: IF both profiles point at the same local workspace or git repository
IF Windsurf auto-edits files while another process also mutates the repo
mitigations: Use separate clones for editing and reference material
Pause other writers before running Windsurf
Commit or stash before agent edits
Disable auto-execute for file-changing commands
requires-engineering: add file-locking around shared repos

D_cascading_error.rationale: Windsurf’s agentic loop can act on generated code or text, and the collection profile can supply reference material that Windsurf may treat as authoritative. Because the collection is not runnable, the main risk is that Windsurf propagates mistaken or malicious snippets into edits or commands without verification. The pathway exists, but there is no evidence of downstream irreversible action by the collection itself.
conditions: IF Windsurf uses imported snippets as facts without verification
IF the operator allows auto-execute or accepts generated commands
mitigations: Require manual review before executing generated commands
Mark imported snippets as untrusted references
Cross-check outputs against source docs
Keep auto-execute disabled
requires-engineering: add citation/verification gates before actions

E_compliance.rationale: Windsurf is closed-source and handles model-provider keys plus workspace files, while the other profile is an open-source collection with no data residency or retention controls. The only concrete compliance issue visible is that sensitive workspace content could be processed by Windsurf’s vendor path; the collection itself does not add a separate residency obligation. This is a gap, but not a documented breach.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in the same workspace used by Windsurf
IF the operator relies on the collection as if it imposed retention or residency controls
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in the Windsurf workspace
Review vendor retention and DPA terms before use
Use a separate environment for regulated projects
Document which data classes may enter the editor
requires-engineering: implement residency-aware routing
